And the people said to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, "Your father made his yoke heavy upon us, and made heavy the provisions of his table; now therefore lighten it upon us, and we will serve you." And Rehoboam said to the people, "Yet three days, and I will answer you a word." And Rehoboam said, "Bring in the elders to me, and I will take counsel with them what word I shall answer the people on the third day." And Rehoboam spoke in their ears just as the people had sent word to him; and the elders of the people said, "Thus the people have spoken to you." And Rehoboam set aside their counsel, and it did not please him; and he sent and brought in his companions, and spoke the same things to them: "These things also the people sent word to me." And his companions said, "Thus you shall speak to the people, saying, 'My littleness is thicker than my father's loins; my father scourged you with whips, but I will rule over you with scorpions.'" And the word pleased Rehoboam; and he answered the people just as his companions, the young men, had counseled him. And all the people spoke as one man, each to his neighbor, and they all cried out, saying, "We have no portion in David, nor inheritance in the son of Jesse! To your tents, O Israel! For this man is neither for a ruler nor for a leader!" And all the people were scattered from Shechem, and every man departed to his tent. And Rehoboam exerted himself, and departed and mounted his chariot and entered into Jerusalem; and all the tribe of Judah and all the tribe of Benjamin went after him. And it came to pass at the turn of the year that Rehoboam gathered every man of Judah and Benjamin, and went up to fight against Jeroboam at Shechem. And the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah the man of God: "Speak to Rehoboam king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the remnant of the people, saying, 'Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up nor fight against your brethren, the children of Israel; return every man to his own house, for this matter has come from Me.'" And they listened to the word of the Lord, and refrained from going, according to the word of the Lord.
verses.12:25: Then Jeroboam built Shechem in Mount Ephraim, and dwelt in it; and he went out from there and built Penuel.
verses.12:26: And Jeroboam said in his heart, "Behold, now the kingdom will return to the house of David.
verses.12:27: If this people goes up to offer sacrifice in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, then the heart of the people will turn back to the Lord and to their lord, to Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will slay me."
verses.12:28: And the king took counsel, and went and made two golden heifers, and said to the people, "Let it be enough for you to go up to Jerusalem! Behold your gods, O Israel, which brought you up out of the land of Egypt!"
verses.12:29: And he set the one in Bethel, and the other he placed in Dan.
verses.12:30: Now this thing became a sin; and the people went before the one, even as far as Dan.
verses.12:31: And he made houses upon high places, and made priests from a portion of the people who were not of the sons of Levi.
verses.12:32: And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast that was in the land of Judah, and he went up to the altar which he had made in Bethel to sacrifice to the heifers which he had made; and he stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places which he had made.
verses.12:33: And he went up to the altar which he had made on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, in the feast which he had devised from his own heart; and he ordained a feast for the children of Israel, and he went up to the altar to offer sacrifice.
verses.13:1: And behold, a man of God from Judah came by the word of the Lord to Bethel, and Jeroboam was standing by the altar to offer sacrifice.
verses.13:2: And he cried out to the altar by the word of the Lord, "Altar, altar, thus says the Lord: 'Behold, a son is born to the house of David, Josiah is his name; and he shall sacrifice upon you the priests of the high places who offer sacrifice upon you, and he shall burn the bones of men upon you.'"
verses.13:3: And he will give a portent on that day, saying, "This is the word which the Lord has spoken, saying, 'Behold, the altar is split apart, and the fatness that is upon it shall be poured out.'"
verses.13:4: And it came to pass, when King Jeroboam heard the words of the man of God who had cried out against the altar that was in Bethel, that the king stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, "Seize him!" And behold, his hand, which he had stretched out against him, withered, and he was not able to draw it back to himself.
verses.13:5: And the altar was split apart, and the fatness was poured out from the altar according to the portent which the man of God had given by the word of the Lord.
verses.13:6: And King Jeroboam said to the man of God, "Implore your God, and let my hand be restored to me." And the man of God implored the face of the Lord, and He restored the king's hand to him, and it became as it was before.
verses.13:7: And the king spoke to the man of God, "Come into the house with me and dine, and I will give you a gift."
verses.13:8: And the man of God said to the king, "If you give me half of your house, I will not go in with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water in this place;
verses.13:9: for thus the Lord commanded me by a word, saying, 'Do not eat bread, and do not drink water, and do not return by the way on which you went.'"
verses.13:10: So he departed by another way, and did not turn back by the way on which he had come to Bethel.
verses.13:11: Now a certain old prophet was dwelling in Bethel; and his sons came and recounted to him all the deeds which the man of God had done that day in Bethel—the words which he had spoken to the king; and they turned the face of their father.
verses.13:12: And their father spoke to them, saying, "By what way has he gone?" And his sons showed him the way by which the man of God who had come from Judah went up.
verses.13:13: And he said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." So they saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it.
verses.13:14: And he went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak. And he said to him, "Are you the man of God who has come from Judah?" And he said to him, "I am."
verses.13:15: Then he said to him, "Come with me and eat bread."
verses.13:16: And he said, "I cannot return with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water in this place;
verses.13:17: for thus the Lord has commanded me by a word, saying, 'Do not eat bread there, and do not drink water, and do not return there by the way on which you went.'"
verses.13:18: And he said to him, "I also am a prophet just as you are, and an angel has spoken to me by the word of the Lord, saying, 'Bring him back to yourself into your house, and let him eat bread and drink water.'" But he lied to him.
verses.13:19: So he brought him back, and he ate bread in his house and drank water.
verses.13:20: And it came to pass, as they were sitting, that the word of the Lord came to the prophet who had brought him back;
verses.13:21: and he said to the man of God who had come from Judah, saying, "Thus says the Lord: Because you have rebelled against the word of the Lord, and have not kept the commandment which the Lord your God commanded you,
verses.13:22: but have turned back and have eaten bread and drunk water in this place of which He spoke to you, saying, 'You shall not eat bread and shall not drink water,' your body shall not enter into the tomb of your fathers."
verses.13:23: And it came to pass, after eating bread and drinking water, that he saddled the donkey for him, and he turned back and departed.
verses.13:24: And a lion met him on the road and put him to death; and his body was cast upon the road, and the donkey was standing beside it, and the lion was standing beside the body.
verses.13:25: And behold, men were passing by, and they saw the corpse cast upon the road, and the lion was standing close beside the corpse; and they entered and spoke of it in the city in which the old prophet dwelt.
verses.13:26: And the one who had brought him back from the road heard it, and said, "This is the man of God who rebelled against the word of the Lord."
verses.13:28: And he went and found his body cast upon the road, and the donkey and the lion were standing beside the body; and the lion had not eaten the body of the man of God, nor had it crushed the donkey.
verses.13:29: And the prophet lifted up the body of the man of God and laid it upon the donkey, and brought him back into the city,
verses.13:30: the prophet himself, to bury him in his own tomb; and they lamented over him, "Alas, brother!"
verses.13:31: And it came to pass, after lamenting him, that he spoke to his sons, saying, "When I die, bury me in this tomb in which the man of God is buried; lay me beside his bones, so that my bones may be saved with his bones.
verses.13:32: For the word which he spoke by the word of the Lord against the altar in Bethel, and against the high houses that are in Samaria, shall surely come to pass."
verses.13:33: And after this matter Jeroboam did not turn back from his wickedness, but turned again and made from a portion of the people priests of high places; whoever desired it, he filled his hand, and he became a priest for the high places.
verses.13:34: And this matter resulted in sin for the house of Jeroboam, and in destruction, and in extermination from the face of the earth.
verses.14:21: Now Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned over Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the Lord had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to place His name there. And his mother's name was Maacham the Ammonitess.
verses.14:22: And Rehoboam did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, and provoked Him to jealousy by all that their fathers had done, in their sins which they had committed.
verses.14:23: And they built for themselves high places and pillars and groves upon every high hill and beneath every shady tree.
verses.14:24: And a conspiracy arose in the land, and they practiced some of all the abominations of the nations whom the Lord had removed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.14:25: And it came to pass in the fifth year of the reign of Rehoboam that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem,
verses.14:26: and he took all the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king's house, and the golden spears which David had taken from the hand of the servants of Hadarezer king of Zobah and brought into Jerusalem—everything, the golden shields which he took.
verses.14:27: And King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place; and the commanders of the runners, who guarded the gateway of the king's house, placed themselves over him.
verses.14:28: And it came to pass, whenever the king entered into the house of the Lord, that the runners would carry them, and then deposit them in the guardroom of the runners.
verses.14:29: Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.14:30: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days.
verses.14:31: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and Abiu his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:1: And in the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abiu son of Jeroboam became king over Judah.
verses.15:2: And he reigned six years; and the name of his mother was Maachah, daughter of Absalom.
verses.15:3: And he walked in the sins of his father which he had committed before him, and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of his father.
verses.15:4: For because of David, the Lord gave him a remnant, that He might establish his children after him and establish Jerusalem,
verses.15:5: since David did what was right in the sight of the Lord; he did not turn aside from all that He commanded him all the days of his life.
verses.15:7: Now the rest of the acts of Abiu, and all that he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the records of the days for the kings of Judah? And there was war between Abiu and Jeroboam.
verses.15:8: And Abiu slept with his fathers in the twenty-fourth year of Jeroboam, and he was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and Asa his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:9: In the twenty-fourth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa became king over Judah,
verses.15:10: and he reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Ana, daughter of Absalom.
verses.15:11: And Asa did what was right in the sight of the Lord, as did David his father.
verses.15:12: And he removed the initiation rites from the land, and banished all the practices which his fathers had practiced.
verses.15:13: And he removed Ana his mother from being ruler, because she had held an assembly in her grove; and Asa cut down her hiding places and burned them with fire in the brook of the cedars.
verses.15:14: But the high places he did not remove; nevertheless, the heart of Asa was perfect with the Lord all his days.
verses.15:15: And he brought in the pillars of his father, and his own pillars he brought into the house of the Lord, of silver and gold, and vessels.
verses.15:16: And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all the days.
verses.15:17: And Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah, and built Ramah, that there might be no one going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.
verses.15:18: Then Asa took the silver and the gold that was found in the treasuries of the king's house, and delivered them into the hands of his servants; and King Asa sent them to the son of Hader, son of Taberema, son of Hazin, king of Syria, who dwelt in Damascus, saying,
verses.15:19: "Make a covenant between me and my father and your father. Behold, I have sent to you gifts of silver and gold. Come, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, and he will withdraw from me."
verses.15:20: So the son of Hader heeded King Asa, and sent the commanders of his forces against the cities of Israel; and they struck Ain, Dan, and Adelmath, and all Chezrath, as far as all the land of Naphtali.
verses.15:21: And it came to pass, when Baasha heard it, that he ceased building Ramah and returned to Tirzah.
verses.15:22: Then King Asa summoned all Judah to Enakim; and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timber, with which Baasha had built, and with them King Asa built every hill of Benjamin and the watchtower.
verses.15:23: Now the rest of the acts of Asa, and all his might which he performed, behold, are they not written in the book of the records of the days for the kings of Judah? Nevertheless, in the time of his old age he was afflicted in his feet.
verses.15:24: So Asa slept, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:25: Now Nebat son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned in Israel two years.
verses.15:26: And he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of his father, and in his sins by which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:27: And Baasha son of Ahijah besieged him at the house of Belaan; and the son of Ahijah struck him down in Gibbethon, which belonged to the foreigners, while Nebat and all Israel were laying siege against Gibbethon.
verses.15:28: And Baasha put him to death in the third year of King Asa son of Abiu, and reigned.
verses.15:29: And it came to pass, when he became king, that he struck down the house of Jeroboam, and did not leave any that breathed of Jeroboam until he had utterly destroyed him, according to the word of the Lord which He spoke by the hand of the servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
verses.15:30: because of the sins of Jeroboam, by which he caused Israel to sin, and because of his provocation with which he provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger.
verses.15:31: Now the rest of the acts of Nebat, and all that he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the records of the days for the kings of Israel?
verses.15:33: And in the third year of the king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over Israel in Tirzah for twenty-four years.
verses.15:34: And he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and in his sins by which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.16:1: And the word of the Lord came by the hand of Jehu son of Hanani to Baasha:
verses.16:2: "Because I exalted you from the earth and appointed you ruler over My people Israel, and you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and have caused My people Israel to sin, to provoke Me to anger with their vanities,
verses.16:3: behold, I will raise up after Baasha and after his house, and I will make his house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
verses.16:4: The one of Baasha who dies in the city, the dogs shall devour him; and the one of his who dies in the field, the birds of heaven shall devour him."
verses.16:5: Now the rest of the acts of Baasha, and all that he did, and his mighty deeds, behold, are they not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:6: So Baasha slept with his fathers, and was buried in Tirzah; and Elah his son reigned in his place in the twentieth year of King Asa.
verses.16:7: And by the hand of Jehu son of Hanani, the Lord spoke against Baasha and against his house concerning all the evil which he did in the sight of the Lord, to provoke Him to anger by the works of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam, and because he had struck it down.
verses.16:8: And Elah son of Baasha reigned over Israel two years in Tirzah.
verses.16:9: And Zimri, the commander of half the cavalry, conspired against him; and he was in Tirzah drinking himself drunk in the house of Osa, the steward in Tirzah.
verses.16:10: And Zimri went in and struck him and put him to death, and reigned in his place.
verses.16:11: And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat upon his throne, that he struck down all the house of Baasha,
verses.16:12: according to the word which the Lord spoke against the house of Baasha and to Jehu the prophet,
verses.16:13: for all the sins of Baasha and of Elah his son, by which he caused Israel to sin, to provoke the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
verses.16:14: Now the rest of the acts of Elah which he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:15: And Zimri reigned seven years in Tirzah; and the camp of Israel was against Gibeon, which belonged to the foreigners.
verses.16:16: And the people in the camp heard it said, "Zimri has conspired and has struck down the king." Therefore in Israel they made Zimri, the commander of the army, king over Israel that very day in the camp.
verses.16:17: Then Zimri, and all Israel with him, went up in Gibbethon and laid siege against Tirzah.
verses.16:18: And it came to pass, when Zimri saw that his city was captured, that they went into the inner vault of the king's house; and the king burned the king's house over him, and he died,
verses.16:19: because of his sins which he committed in doing what was evil in the sight of the Lord, in walking in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and in his sins by which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.16:20: Now the rest of the acts of Zimri, and his conspiracies which he formed, behold, are they not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:21: Then the people of Israel were divided: half of the people followed Tibni son of Ginath to make him king, and half of the people followed Zimri.
verses.16:22: And the people who followed Tibni son of Ginath were defeated; and Tibni died, and Joram his brother at that time, and Zimri reigned after Tibni.
verses.16:23: In the thirty-first year of King Asa, Zimri became king over Israel for twelve years; in Tirzah he reigned six years.
verses.16:24: And Zimri bought the mountain of Samaria from Shemer, the owner of the mountain, for two talents of silver; and he built on the mountain, and they called the name of the mountain which they built, after the name of Shemer the owner of the mountain, Samaria.
verses.16:25: And Zimri did what was evil in the sight of the Lord; he acted more wickedly than all who were before him.
verses.16:26: And he walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and in his sins by which he caused Israel to sin, to provoke to anger with their vanities.
verses.16:27: Now the rest of the acts of Zimri, and all that he did, and his might, behold, are they not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:28: So Zimri slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria; and Ahab his son reigned in his place. And in the eleventh year of Zimri, Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king; he was thirty-five years old when he began his reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Gabuza, daughter of Selei. And he walked in the way of Asa his father, and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the sight of the Lord; yet they did not remove the high places; they sacrificed and burned incense on the high places. Now the alliances which Jehoshaphat made, and all the might which he showed, and those with whom he waged war, behold, are they not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Judah? And the remainder of the corrupt unions which they had undertaken in the days of Asa his father, he removed from the land. And there was no king in Syria; Nasib was the king. He built a ship for Tarshish to go to Sophir, to go for gold; but it did not go, for the ship was shattered at Ezion Geber. Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will send forth your servants and my young men in the ship." But Jehoshaphat was not willing. And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers in the city of David; and Joram his son reigned in his place.
verses.16:29: In the second year of Jehoshaphat, Ahab son of Zimri became king; he reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
verses.16:30: And Ahab did what was evil in the sight of the Lord; he acted more wickedly than all who were before him.
verses.16:31: And it was not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, but he took as his wife Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians; and he went and served Baal and worshiped him.
verses.16:32: And he set up an altar to Baal in the house of his abominations, which he had built in Samaria.
verses.16:33: And Ahab made a grove; and Ahab did even more to commit provocations to provoke his own soul, so as to be utterly destroyed; he did more evil than all the kings of Israel who were before him.
verses.16:34: Hiel the Bethelite built Jericho; at the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the cost of Segub his youngest he set up its gates, according to the word of the Lord which He spoke by the hand of Joshua son of Nun.
verses.17:1: And Elijah the prophet, the Tishbite from Tishbe of Gilead, said to Ahab, "As the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I have stood, there shall not be dew or rain these years, except by the mouth of my word."
verses.17:2: And the word of the Lord came to Elijah:
verses.17:3: "Depart from here toward the east, and hide yourself by the brook Cherith, which is before the Jordan.
verses.17:4: And it shall be that you shall drink water from the brook, and I will command the ravens to sustain you there."
verses.17:5: And Elijah did according to the word of the Lord, and dwelt by the brook Cherith before the Jordan.
verses.17:6: And the ravens brought him loaves of bread in the morning and meat in the evening, and he drank water from the brook.
verses.17:7: And it came to pass after some days that the brook dried up, because there had been no rain upon the earth.
verses.17:8: And the word of the Lord came to Elijah:
verses.17:9: "Arise and go to Zarephath of Sidon; behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain you."
verses.17:10: So he arose and went to Zarephath, to the gate of the city; and behold, a widow woman was there gathering sticks. And Elijah called out after her and said to her, "Please fetch a little water in a vessel, and I will drink."
verses.17:11: And she went to fetch it, and Elijah called out after her and said, "Please bring me a morsel of the bread that is in your hand."
verses.17:12: And the woman said, "As the Lord your God lives, I have no baked cake, only as much as a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the flask. And behold, I am gathering two sticks, and I will go in and prepare it for myself and my children, and we shall eat, and we shall die."
verses.17:13: And Elijah said to her, "Take courage; go in and do according to your word. Only make for me from it a small baked cake first and bring it out to me, and afterward you shall make some for yourself and your children,
verses.17:14: for thus says the Lord: 'The jar of flour shall not fail, nor shall the flask of oil diminish, until the day the Lord gives rain upon the earth.'"
verses.17:15: So the woman went and did so; and she ate, and he, and her children.
verses.17:16: And the jar of flour did not fail, nor did the flask of oil diminish, according to the word of the Lord which He spoke by the hand of Elijah.
verses.17:17: And it came to pass after these things that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick; and his sickness was exceedingly severe, until there was no breath left in him.
verses.17:18: And she said to Elijah, "What have I to do with you, O man of God? Have you come in to me to bring my iniquity to remembrance and to put my son to death?"
verses.17:19: And Elijah said to the woman, "Give me your son." And he took him from her bosom and carried him up to the upper room where he himself was staying, and laid him upon the bed.
verses.17:20: And Elijah cried aloud and said, "Alas, O Lord, the witness of the widow with whom I dwell, You have brought evil upon her by putting her son to death!"
verses.17:21: And he breathed upon the child three times, and called upon the Lord and said, "O Lord my God, I pray, let the soul of this child return into him."
verses.17:22: And so it came to pass, and the child cried out.
verses.17:23: And he brought him down from the upper room into the house and gave him to his mother. And Elijah said, "Look, your son lives."
verses.17:24: And the woman said to Elijah, "Behold, I know that you are a man of God, and the word of the Lord in your mouth is true."
verses.18:1: And it came to pass after many days that the word of the Lord came to Elijah in the third year, saying, "Go and show yourself to Ahab, and I will give rain upon the face of the earth."
verses.18:2: So Elijah went to show himself to Ahab, and the famine was severe in Samaria.
verses.18:3: And Ahab called Obadiah the steward; now Obadiah feared the Lord exceedingly.
verses.18:4: For it came to pass, when Jezebel was striking down the prophets of the Lord, that Obadiah took one hundred men who were prophets and hid them by fifties in a cave, and sustained them with bread and water.
verses.18:5: And Ahab said to Obadiah, "Come, and let us pass through the land to the springs of water and to the brooks; perhaps we may find grass and preserve the horses and mules alive, and they shall not be destroyed from the tents."
verses.18:6: So they divided the way between themselves to pass through it: Ahab went by one way, and Obadiah went by another way alone.
verses.18:7: Now Obadiah was on the way alone, and Elijah came alone to meet him; and Obadiah hastened and fell upon his face and said, "Is it indeed you, my lord Elijah?"
verses.18:8: And Elijah said to him, "It is I. Go, tell your lord, 'Behold, Elijah!'"
verses.18:9: And Obadiah said, "How have I sinned, that you are delivering your servant into the hand of Ahab to put me to death?
verses.18:10: As the Lord your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to seek you; and when they said, 'He is not here,' he even burned the kingdom and its regions because he had not found you.
verses.18:11: And now you say, 'Go, report to your lord.'
verses.18:12: And it shall come to pass, as soon as I depart from you, that the Spirit of the Lord will carry you away to a land that I do not know; and I will go in to report to Ahab, and he will slay me. Yet your servant has feared the Lord from his youth.
verses.18:13: Was it not reported to you, my lord, what I did when Jezebel was slaying the prophets of the Lord, how I hid one hundred men of the prophets of the Lord, fifty to a cave, and fed them with loaves of bread and water?
verses.18:14: And now you say to me, 'Go, tell your lord, "Behold, Elijah!"' and he will slay me."
verses.18:15: And Elijah said, "As the Lord of hosts lives, before whom I have stood, today I will surely show myself to him."
verses.18:16: So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and reported to him; and Ahab ran out and went to meet Elijah.
verses.18:17: And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said to Elijah, "Are you yourself the one who perverts Israel?"
verses.18:18: And Elijah said, "I do not pervert Israel, but rather you and the house of your father, in that you have forsaken the Lord your God, and you have gone after the Baals.
verses.18:19: Now therefore send and gather to me all Israel to Mount Carmel, and the prophets of shame, four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the groves, four hundred, who eat at the table of Jezebel."
verses.18:20: So Ahab sent throughout all Israel, and gathered all the prophets together to Mount Carmel.
verses.18:21: And Elijah drew near to all of them, and Elijah said to them, "How long will you limp on both knees? If the Lord is God, follow after Him; but if Baal, follow after him." And the people did not answer a word.
verses.18:22: Then Elijah said to the people, "I alone am left a prophet of the Lord, while the prophets of Baal are four hundred and fifty men, and the prophets of the grove are four hundred.
verses.18:23: Let them give us two oxen, and let them choose one for themselves, and cut it in pieces and lay it on the wood, and put no fire to it; and I will prepare the other ox, and I will by no means put fire to it.
verses.18:24: And cry out in the name of your gods, and I will call upon the name of the Lord my God; and it shall be that the God who answers by fire, He is God." And all the people answered and said, "Good is the word which you have spoken."
verses.18:25: And Elijah said to the prophets of shame, "Choose for yourselves one bullock and prepare it first, for you are many; and call upon the name of your god, and put no fire to it."
verses.18:26: So they took the bullock and prepared it, and called upon the name of Baal from morning until midday, and said, "Hear us, O Baal, hear us!" But there was no voice and no hearing; and they ran about upon the altar which they had made.
verses.18:27: And midday came, and Elijah the Tishbite mocked them and said, "Call out with a loud voice, for he is a god! For he is occupied in conversation, and perhaps at the same time he is conducting business, or perhaps he is sleeping and will wake up!"
verses.18:28: So they called out with a loud voice, and cut themselves with knife and lances until blood gushed out upon them,
verses.18:29: and they prophesied until the afternoon had passed. And it came to pass, about the time for the sacrifice to be offered up, that Elijah spoke to the prophets of the abominations, saying, "Stand aside from now on, and I will prepare my burnt offering." And they stood aside and departed.
verses.18:30: Then Elijah said to the people, "Draw near to me." And all the people drew near to him.
verses.18:31: And Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of Israel, as the Lord spoke to him, saying, "Israel shall be your name."
verses.18:32: And he built the stones in the name of the Lord, and repaired the altar that had been torn down; and he made a sea around the altar, holding two measures of seed.
verses.18:33: And he stacked the split wood upon the altar which he had made, and cut the burnt offering in pieces, and laid on the split wood, and stacked it upon the altar.
verses.18:34: And he said, "Fetch me four jars of water, and pour it upon the burnt offering and upon the split wood." And they did so. And he said, "Do it a second time," and they did it a second time. And he said, "Do it a third time," and they did it a third time.
verses.18:35: And the water ran all around the altar, and they filled the sea with water.
verses.18:36: And Elijah cried aloud to heaven and said, "O Lord, the God of Abraham and Isaac and Israel, hear me, O Lord, hear me today by fire, and let all this people know that You are the Lord, the God of Israel, and I am Your servant, and for Your sake I have done these works.
verses.18:37: Hear me, O Lord, hear me, that this people may know that You are the Lord God, and that You have turned the heart of this people back again."
verses.18:38: Then fire fell from the Lord out of heaven, and devoured the burnt offerings and the split wood and the water that was in the sea, and the fire licked up the stones and the dust.
verses.18:39: And all the people fell upon their faces and said, "Truly, the Lord is God; He is God!"
verses.18:40: And Elijah said to the people, "Seize the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape!" So they seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the brook Kishon and slaughtered them there.
verses.18:41: And Elijah said to Ahab, "Go up, and eat and drink, for there is the sound of the feet of the rain."
verses.18:42: So Ahab went up to eat and to drink; and Elijah went up to Carmel, and bowed down to the earth and put his face between his knees,
verses.18:43: and he said to his young servant, "Go up and look toward the sea." And the young servant looked and said, "There is nothing." And Elijah said, "Turn back seven times, and return seven times."
verses.18:44: And the young servant returned seven times; and it came to pass at the seventh time that behold, a small cloud like a man's footprint was bringing up water. And he said, "Go up and say to Ahab, 'Harness your chariot and go down, lest the rain overtake you.'"
verses.18:45: And it came to pass meanwhile that the heaven grew dark with clouds and wind, and the rain became great; and Ahab wept and went to Israel.
verses.18:46: And the hand of the Lord was upon Elijah; and he girded up his loins, and ran before Ahab to Israel.
verses.19:1: And Ahab reported to Jezebel his wife all that Elijah had done, and how he had slain the prophets with the sword.
verses.19:2: And Jezebel sent to Elijah and said, "If you are Elijah and I am Jezebel, may God do these things to me, and more also, that at this hour tomorrow I will make your life like the life of one of them."
verses.19:3: And Elijah was afraid, and he arose and departed for his own life; and he came to Beersheba, the land of Judah, and left his young servant there.
verses.19:4: And he himself went a day's journey into the wilderness, and came and sat down beneath a broom tree. And he asked for his own life that he might die, and said, "Let it be enough now! Take now my life from me, O Lord, for I am no better than my fathers."
verses.19:5: And he lay down and slept there under a shrub; and behold, someone touched him and said to him, "Arise and eat."
verses.19:6: And Elijah looked, and behold, by his head was a hearth cake of spelt and a flask of water. And he arose and ate and drank, and turning back, he lay down again.
verses.19:7: And the angel of the Lord returned a second time, and touched him, and said to him, "Arise, eat, for the journey is too great for you."
verses.19:8: And he arose and ate and drank; and he went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights as far as Mount Horeb.
verses.19:9: And he entered into the cave there and lodged there; and behold, the word of the Lord came to him, and He said, "Why are you here, Elijah?"
verses.19:10: And Elijah said, "With zeal I have been zealous for the Lord Almighty, because the sons of Israel have forsaken You; Your altars they have torn down, and Your prophets they have slain with the sword. And I alone am left, and they seek my life, to take it."
verses.19:11: And He said, "You shall go forth tomorrow and stand before the Lord on the mountain; behold, the Lord will pass by." And there was a great and mighty wind tearing apart mountains and shattering rocks before the Lord, in the wind of the Lord; and after the wind an earthquake, yet the Lord was not in the earthquake;
verses.19:12: and after the earthquake a fire, yet the Lord was not in the fire; and after the fire, the sound of a gentle breeze.
verses.19:13: And it came to pass, when Elijah heard it, that he covered his face with his sheepskin mantle, and went out and stood beneath the cave. And behold, a voice came to him and said, "Why are you here, Elijah?"
verses.19:14: And Elijah said, "With zeal I have been zealous for the Lord Almighty, because the sons of Israel have forsaken You; Your covenant and Your altars they have pulled down, and Your prophets they have slain with the sword. And I alone am left, and they seek my life, to take it."
verses.19:15: And the Lord said to him, "Go, return on your way, and you shall come to the way of the wilderness of Damascus; and you shall come and anoint Hazael to be king of Syria;
verses.19:16: and the son of Jehu, the son of Nimshi, you shall anoint to be king over Israel; and Elisha the son of Shaphat, from Abel Meholah, you shall anoint as prophet in your place.
verses.19:17: And it shall come to pass that whoever escapes from the sword of Hazael, Jehu shall put to death; and whoever escapes from the sword of Jehu, Elisha shall put to death.
verses.19:18: And you shall leave in Israel seven thousand men—all the knees that have not bowed the knee to Baal, and every mouth that has not worshiped him."
verses.19:19: And he departed from there and found Elisha the son of Shaphat, while he was plowing with oxen, twelve yoke before him, and he was among the twelve. And he came up to him and cast his sheepskin mantle upon him.
verses.19:20: And Elisha left the oxen and ran after Elijah, and said, "Let me kiss my father, and I will follow after you." And Elijah said, "Return, for I have done this to you."
verses.19:21: And he turned back from following him, and took the yokes of oxen and slaughtered them, and boiled them with the gear of the oxen, and gave them to the people, and they ate. Then he arose and went after Elijah, and ministered to him.
verses.20:1: And Naboth the Israelite had a certain vineyard beside the threshing floor of Ahab king of Samaria.
verses.20:2: And Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, "Give me your vineyard, and it shall be for me a garden of herbs, because it is near to my house, and I will give you another vineyard better than it; or if it is pleasing in your sight, I will give you silver in exchange for this vineyard of yours, and it shall be for me a garden of herbs."
verses.20:3: And Naboth said to Ahab, "Far be it from me, by my God, to give the inheritance of my fathers to you."
verses.20:4: And the spirit of Ahab became troubled, and he lay down upon his bed and covered his face, and did not eat bread.
verses.20:5: And Jezebel his wife came in to him and spoke to him, "Why is your spirit troubled, and why are you not eating bread?"
verses.20:6: And he said to her, "Because I spoke to Naboth the Israelite, saying, 'Give me your vineyard for silver; or if you wish, I will give you another vineyard in its place.' And he said, 'I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers.'"
verses.20:7: And Jezebel his wife said to him, "Do you now act the king over Israel like this? Arise, eat bread, and be yourself again; I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Israelite."
verses.20:8: And she wrote a letter in the name of Ahab and sealed it with his seal, and sent the letter to the elders and the free men who dwelt with Naboth.
verses.20:9: And it was written in the letters, saying, "Observe a fast, and seat Naboth at the head of the people;
verses.20:10: and set two men, sons of lawless men."
verses.20:11: And the men of his city, the elders and the free men who dwelt in his city, did just as Jezebel had sent to them, and according to what was written in the letters that she had sent to them.
verses.20:12: And they proclaimed a fast, and seated Naboth at the head of the people.
verses.20:13: And they sat opposite him, and testified against him, saying, "You have blessed God and the king." And they brought him outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.
verses.20:14: And they sent to Jezebel, saying, "Naboth has been stoned and is dead."
verses.20:15: And it came to pass, when Jezebel heard, that she said to Ahab, "Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Israelite, who did not give it to you for silver; for Naboth is not alive, for he is dead."
verses.20:16: And it came to pass, when Ahab heard that Naboth the Israelite was dead, that he tore his garments and put on sackcloth. And it came to pass after these things that Ahab arose and went down to the vineyard of Naboth the Israelite to take possession of it.
verses.20:17: And the Lord said to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
verses.20:18: "Arise and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria, for he is in the vineyard of Naboth, because he has gone down there to take possession of it.
verses.20:19: And you shall speak to him, saying, 'Thus says the Lord: Since you have murdered and also taken possession, therefore thus says the Lord: In every place where the swine and the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, there the dogs shall lick your blood, and the harlots shall wash themselves in your blood.'"
verses.20:20: And Ahab said to Elijah, "Have you found me, O my enemy?" And he said, "I have found you, because you have sold yourself in vain to do evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke Him to anger.
verses.20:21: Behold, I am bringing calamity upon you, and I will burn up those after you, and I will utterly destroy from Ahab every one who urinates against a wall, both the confined and the forsaken in Israel;
verses.20:22: and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah, because of the provocations with which you have provoked to anger and have caused Israel to sin."
verses.20:23: And concerning Jezebel the Lord spoke, saying, "The dogs shall devour her in the rampart of Israel.
verses.20:24: Whoever of Ahab dies in the city, the dogs shall eat; and whoever of his dies in the field, the birds of the sky shall eat."
verses.20:25: Yet in vain did Ahab act, in that he sold himself to do evil in the sight of the Lord, as Jezebel his wife led him astray;
verses.20:26: and he acted exceedingly abominably in going after the abominations, according to all that the Amorite had done, whom the Lord utterly destroyed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.20:27: And because of the word, when Ahab was pierced to the heart before the Lord, he went about weeping, and tore his tunic, and girded sackcloth upon his body, and fasted; and he put on sackcloth on the day he struck down Naboth the Israelite, and went his way.
verses.20:28: And the word of the Lord came by the hand of His servant Elijah concerning Ahab, and the Lord said,
verses.20:29: "Have you seen how Ahab has been pierced to the heart before Me? I will not bring the calamity in his days, but in the days of his son I will bring the calamity."
verses.21:1: And Son of Hader gathered all his army and went up and besieged Samaria, and thirty-two kings with him, and every horse and chariot; and they went up and besieged Samaria, and fought against it.
verses.21:2: And he sent to Ahab king of Israel into the city, and said to him, "Thus says Son of Hader:
verses.21:3: 'Your silver and your gold are mine, and your wives and your children are mine.'"
verses.21:4: And the king of Israel answered and said, "Just as you have spoken, O lord king, I am yours, and all that is mine."
verses.21:5: And the messengers returned and said, "Thus says Son of Hader: 'I sent back, saying: Your silver and your gold and your wives you shall give to me;
verses.21:6: for at this hour tomorrow I will send my servants to you, and they shall search your house and the houses of your servants; and it shall be that the desirable things of their eyes, upon which they lay their hands, they shall take.'"
verses.21:7: And the king of Israel called all the elders and said, "Know now and see that this man seeks evil; for he has sent to me concerning my wives, and concerning my sons, and concerning my daughters; my silver and my gold I did not withhold from him."
verses.21:8: And the elders and all the people said to him, "Do not listen, and do not consent."
verses.21:9: And he said to the messengers of Son of Hader, "Tell your lord, 'All that you sent for to your servant at the first I will do, but this thing I shall not be able to do.'" And the men departed and brought back word to him.
verses.21:10: And Son of Hader sent to him, saying, "Thus may God do to me, and thus may He add, if the dust of Samaria shall suffice for the foxes for all the people, my foot soldiers."
verses.21:11: And the king of Israel answered and said, "Let it suffice; do not let the hunchbacked boast like the upright."
verses.21:12: And it came to pass, when he answered him this word, that he was drinking, he and all the kings with him, in tents; and he said to his servants, "Build a palisade." And they set a palisade against the city.
verses.21:13: And behold, a certain prophet came near to the king of Israel and said, "Thus says the Lord: 'Have you seen this great multitude? Behold, I deliver it today into your hands, and you shall know that I am the Lord.'"
verses.21:14: And Ahab said, "By whom?" And he said, "Thus says the Lord: 'By the young men of the rulers of the provinces.'" And Ahab said, "Who shall join the battle?" And he said, "You."
verses.21:15: And Ahab mustered the rulers, the young men of the provinces, and they were two hundred and thirty; and after these things he mustered the people, every son of might, sixty.
verses.21:16: And he went out at noon. And Son of Hader was drinking himself drunk in Succoth, he and the kings, thirty-two, allied kings with him.
verses.21:17: And the rulers, the young men of the provinces, went out first. And they sent and reported to the king of Syria, saying, "Men have come out from Samaria."
verses.21:18: "Tell them, for peace—for they do not come out—seize them alive; and for war, seize them alive;
verses.21:19: and do not let the ruling young men, the rulers of the provinces, come out from the city, and the army behind them."
verses.21:20: Each one struck the man beside him, and each one struck the man beside him a second time, and Syria fled; and Israel pursued them, and Son of Hader, king of Syria, escaped on a horseman's horse.
verses.21:21: And the king of Israel went out and took all the horses and the chariots, and struck a great blow in Syria.
verses.21:22: And the prophet came near to the king of Israel and said, "Be strong, and know and see what you shall do; for at the return of the year Son of Hader, king of Syria, is coming up against you."
verses.21:23: And the servants of the king of Syria said, "A God of the mountains is the God of Israel, and not a God of the valley; therefore He prevailed over us. But if we fight them on level ground, surely we shall prevail over them.
verses.21:24: And do this thing: remove the kings, each one to their own place, and set satraps instead of them,
verses.21:25: and we will replace for you an army like the army that fell, and horse for horse, and chariots for chariots; and we will fight against them on level ground, and we shall prevail over them." And he listened to his voice, and did so.
verses.21:26: And it came to pass at the return of the year that Son of Hader mustered Syria, and went up to Aphek to war against Israel.
verses.21:27: And the sons of Israel were mustered, and came to meet them; and Israel encamped opposite them like two flocks of goats, while Syria filled the land.
verses.21:28: And the man of God came near and said to the king of Israel, "Thus says the Lord: 'Because Syria has said that the Lord, the God of Israel, is a God of the mountains, and He is not a God of the valleys, I will deliver this great army into your hand, and you shall know that I am the Lord;
verses.21:29: and these shall encamp opposite those for seven days.'" And it came to pass on the seventh day that the battle drew near, and Israel struck Syria, one hundred thousand foot soldiers in one day.
verses.21:30: And the rest fled to Aphek, into the city; and the wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand men of those who remained. And Son of Hader fled and entered into the house of the bedchamber, into the inner room.
verses.21:31: And he said to his servants, "I know that the kings of Israel are kings of mercy; let us now put sackcloth upon our loins and ropes upon our heads, and let us still go out to the king of Israel, if perhaps he will preserve our lives."
verses.21:32: So they girded sackcloth around their loins and put ropes upon their heads, and said to the king of Israel, "Your servant Son of Hader says, 'Let our soul live, I pray.'" And he said, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."
verses.21:33: And the men took it as an omen and made a truce, and caught up the word from his mouth and said, "Your brother is Son of Hader." And he said, "Go in and bring him." And Son of Hader came out to him, and they brought him up to him onto the chariot.
verses.21:34: And he said to him, "The cities which my father took from your father I will restore to you, and you shall establish outlets for yourself in Damascus, just as my father established in Samaria." "And I will send you away with a covenant." And he made a covenant with him, and sent him away.
verses.21:35: Now a certain man of the sons of the prophets said to his neighbor by the word of the Lord, "Strike me, I pray." And the man was not willing to strike him.
verses.21:36: Then he said to him, "Because you have not listened to the voice of the Lord, behold, as you go away from me, a lion shall strike you." And he departed from him, and a lion found him and struck him.
verses.21:37: And he found another man and said, "Strike me, I pray." And the man struck him; striking him, he bruised him.
verses.21:38: And the prophet went and stood waiting for the king of Israel on the road, and bound up his eyes with a bandage.
verses.21:39: And it came to pass, as the king was passing by, that this man cried out to the king and said, "Your servant went out to the campaign of the war, and behold, a man brought a man out to me and said to me, 'Guard this man; and if he escapes at all, then your life shall be for his life, or you shall weigh out a talent of silver.'
verses.21:40: And it came to pass that your servant looked around here and there, and he was not there." And the king of Israel said to him, "Behold, you have even slain the ambushes beside me."
verses.21:41: And he hastened and removed the bandage from his eyes; and the king of Israel recognized him, that he was of the prophets.
verses.21:42: And he said to him, "Thus says the Lord: 'Because you have let go out of your hand a destructive man, therefore your life shall be for his life, and your people for his people.'"
verses.21:43: And the king of Israel departed, confounded and dispirited, and came to Samaria.
verses.22:1: And he remained three years, and there was no war between Syria and Israel.
verses.22:2: And it came to pass in the third year that Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to the king of Israel.
verses.22:3: And the king of Israel said to his servants, "Do you know that Ramoth Gilead belongs to us, yet we keep silent from taking it out of the hand of the king of Syria?"
verses.22:4: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you go up with us to Ramoth Gilead to battle?"
verses.22:5: And Jehoshaphat said, "As I am, so are you; as my people are, so are your people; as my horses are, so are your horses." And Jehoshaphat king of Judah said to the king of Israel, "Please inquire today of the Lord."
verses.22:6: Then the king of Israel gathered together all the prophets, about four hundred men, and the king said to them, "Shall I go to Ramoth Gilead to battle, or shall I refrain?" And they said, "Go up, and the Lord will surely deliver it into the hands of the king."
verses.22:7: And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Is there not a prophet of the Lord here, that we may inquire of the Lord through him?"
verses.22:8: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is one man through whom to inquire of the Lord, yet I hate him, because he does not speak good concerning me, but only evil—Micaiah the son of Jemiah." And Jehoshaphat king of Judah said, "Do not let the king speak thus."
verses.22:9: Then the king of Israel summoned a eunuch and said, "Quickly, Micaiah the son of Jemiah!"
verses.22:10: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting each man upon his throne, armed, in the gates of Samaria; and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
verses.22:11: And Zedekiah the son of Chaana made horns of iron for himself and said, "Thus says the Lord: 'With these you shall gore Syria until it is consumed.'"
verses.22:12: And all the prophets were prophesying in this manner, saying, "Go up to Ramoth Gilead, and it shall prosper; and the Lord will deliver even the king of Syria into your hands."
verses.22:13: And the messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah spoke to him, saying, "Behold now, all the prophets speak with one mouth for good concerning the king. Now let you also be in agreement in your words, like the words of one of these, and speak good."
verses.22:14: And Micaiah said, "As the Lord lives, whatever the Lord says to me, that I will speak."
verses.22:15: And he came to the king, and the king said to him, "Micaiah, shall I go up to Ramoth Gilead to battle, or shall I refrain?" And he said, "Go up, and the Lord will prosper it into the hand of the king."
verses.22:16: And the king said to him, "Five times I adjure you that you speak to me the truth in the name of the Lord."
verses.22:17: And he said, "Not so! I have seen all Israel scattered upon the mountains like a flock that has no shepherd. And the Lord said, 'Is the Lord not God to these? Let each one return to his house in peace.'"
verses.22:18: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Did I not say to you, 'This man does not prophesy good to me, but only evil'?"
verses.22:19: And Micaiah said, "Not so! Not I! Hear the word of the Lord! Not so! I saw the God of Israel sitting upon His throne, and all the host of heaven stood around Him, on His right hand and on His left.
verses.22:20: And the Lord said, 'Who will deceive Ahab king of Israel, so that he will go up and fall at Ramoth Gilead?' And one spoke in this manner, and another in that manner.
verses.22:21: And a spirit came forth and stood before the Lord, and said, 'I will deceive him.'
verses.22:22: And the Lord said to him, 'By what means?' And he said, 'I will go forth and become a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And He said, 'You shall deceive him, and you shall also prevail. Go forth and do so.'
verses.22:23: And now, behold, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and the Lord has spoken evil against you."
verses.22:24: Then Zedekiah the son of Canaan came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek, and said, "What spirit of the Lord is it that has spoken in you?"
verses.22:25: And Micaiah said, "Behold, you shall see on that day when you enter into a chamber of the hidden chamber."
verses.22:26: And the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and return him to Semer the king of the city, and to Joash the son of the king
verses.22:27: say to place this man in prison, and for him to eat bread of affliction and water of affliction until I return in peace."
verses.22:28: And Micaiah said, "If you indeed return in peace, the Lord has not spoken by me."
verses.22:29: So the king of Israel went up, and Jehoshaphat king of Judah with him, to Ramoth Gilead.
verses.22:30: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "I will disguise myself and enter into the battle, but you put on my robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself and entered into the battle.
verses.22:31: Now the king of Syria had commanded the thirty-two commanders of his chariots, saying, "Do not fight with small or great, but with the king of Israel alone."
verses.22:32: And it came to pass, when the commanders of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat king of Judah, that they said, "This appears to be the king of Israel." And they surrounded him to fight; and Jehoshaphat cried out.
verses.22:33: And it came to pass, when the commanders of the chariots saw that this was not the king of Israel, that they turned back from him.
verses.22:34: And a certain man drew his bow with good aim and struck the king of Israel between the lung and the breastplate. So he said to his charioteer, "Turn your hands around and bring me out of the battle, for I am wounded."
verses.22:35: And the battle turned on that day; and the king stood upright in the chariot facing Syria from morning until evening, and blood poured out from the wound into the hollow of the chariot. And he died in the evening, and the blood of the rout flowed out to the hollow of the chariot.
verses.22:36: And the herald of the army stood at the setting of the sun, saying, "Every man to his own city and to his own land,
verses.22:37: for the king is dead!" And they came to Samaria, and buried the king in Samaria.
verses.22:38: And they washed off the blood at the spring of Samaria, and the swine and the dogs licked up the blood, and the harlots bathed in the blood, according to the word of the Lord which He had spoken.
verses.22:39: Now the rest of the acts of Ahab, and all that he did, and the ivory house which he built, and all the cities which he made, behold, these are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.22:40: So Ahab slept with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.22:41: And Jehoshaphat the son of Asa began to reign over Judah; in the fourth year of Ahab he began to reign.
verses.22:42: Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Azaeba, the daughter of Shimei.
verses.22:43: And he walked in all the way of Asa his father; he did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the Lord.
verses.22:44: Nevertheless, he did not remove the high places; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
verses.22:45: And Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
verses.22:46: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and his mighty deeds, all that he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the records of Jehoshaphat?
verses.22:51: And he slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David his father; and Joram his son reigned in his place.
verses.22:52: And Ahaziah the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned in Israel two years.
verses.22:53: And he did what was evil before the Lord, and walked in the way of his father Ahab, and in the way of Jezebel his mother, and in the sins of the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
verses.22:54: And he served the Baals and worshiped them, and provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger according to all that had taken place before him. And Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab.

notes.1:8: The Greek text reads "the mighty sons of David" rather than the Hebrew "mighty men who belonged to David," and transliterates Rei as Resei.
notes.1:9: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "by the Stone of Zoheleth, which is by En Rogel," the Septuagint renders a personal name and designation, "with Aithe of Zoheleth, who was beside Rogel," and calls the invited guests "the notable men of Judah."
notes.1:36: Following the Greek text, Benaiah prays that "the God of my lord the king" may "confirm" the royal decree, rather than the Hebrew "so may the LORD, the God of my lord the king, say."
notes.1:40: The Greek text reads "danced in dances," reflecting a Hebrew root for dancing, whereas the Masoretic Text reads "played on flutes."
notes.1:48: The Greek text preserves the phrase "from my seed" before "sitting upon my throne," underscoring David's dynastic succession.
notes.2:6: The Septuagint omits the negative particle found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, reading literally "and you shall bring down his gray hair in peace to Hades."
notes.2:34: The Septuagint reads "Jehoiada" alone here, omitting "Benaiah the son of" before his name.
notes.2:35: The Septuagint includes an extended miscellany summarizing Solomon's wisdom, building works, and David's charge regarding Shimei (here placed "from Hebron" rather than Bahurim), with LXX-distinct names Assur (for Hazor), Magao (for Megiddo), and Upper Beth-horon (for Lower Beth-horon).
notes.2:39: The Septuagint names Achish's father "Amesa" rather than "Maacah" as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.2:46: The Septuagint appends an extensive summary of Solomon's reign, royal provisions, territory, and officials, featuring LXX-distinct names including Thermai (for Tadmor/Tamar), Raphi (for Tiphsah), and the officers Orniou, Suba, Baasha son of Achithalam, Abi son of Joab, Achire son of Edrai, and Kachur son of Nathan.
notes.3:2: The Septuagint lacks verse 1 here (placing Solomon's marriage to Pharaoh's daughter elsewhere) and opens verse 2 abruptly with the participle "burning incense" (thymiontes).
notes.3:15: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the Greek specifies that Solomon stood before the altar that was before the ark of the covenant "in Zion," and that he prepared a great banquet "for himself" as well as all his servants.
notes.3:17: "O my lord" renders the literal Greek idiom en emoi, kyrie ("in me, lord"), a Hebraizing expression of respectful entreaty (also in 3:26).
notes.3:27: The Septuagint uniquely embeds the true mother's plea directly within Solomon's verdict ("to her who said, 'Give him to her...'").
notes.4:2: Throughout Solomon's cabinet list (vv. 2-6), the Septuagint preserves several distinct personal names compared to the Hebrew text—including Azari (v. 2), Eliaph, Saba, and Ahiliad (v. 3), Ornia (v. 5), and Ahi, Eliak, Eliab son of Saph, and Ephra (v. 6)—and omits Benaiah from verse 4.
notes.4:9: Numerous district officers and place names in verses 8-16 differ substantially from the Hebrew text, including Baior (v. 8); Rechas, Machemas, Bethalami, Elom, and Bethlaman (v. 9); Bakcha son of Ahimach, Polamach, the house of Dan, Sesathan, Esrae, Baisaphut, Ebelmaola, and Maeber Lukam (v. 12); Eretabam (v. 13); Ahinaab son of Achel (v. 14); and Maala (v. 16).
notes.4:10: "Bernemalusamencha and Respharachein" are untranslated Greek transliterations of Hebrew geographic phrases (corresponding to "in Arubboth; to him belonged Socoh and the land of Hepher"), and "throughout Dan and throughout Phathei, the husband of Tablethei" in verse 11 likewise reflects a distinct Greek form.
notes.4:17: The Septuagint arranges the final three districts differently from the Hebrew text (vv. 17-19), omits the personal name "Shimei" before "the son of Elah" in verse 17, and reads "Phuasud" (for Hebrew Paruah) in verse 19.
notes.4:18: The Greek reads "the son of Adai in the land of Gad" and "king of Heshbon" (where the Hebrew has "Geber the son of Uri in the land of Gilead" and "king of the Amorites"), and leaves the Hebrew word for "officer" untranslated as naseph.
notes.5:11: The Greek preserves distinct proper-name forms—Gaithan the Zareite, Ainan, Chalkad, and Darala—and reads the singular 'the son of Mal' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol.'
notes.5:12: The Greek reads 'five thousand' songs, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'one thousand and five.'
notes.5:14: In the Septuagint, this verse joins Solomon's marriage to Pharaoh's daughter and Pharaoh's capture of Gezer and Mergab (an LXX-distinct place name) directly to the notice of Solomon's renown, whereas the Hebrew places those events in chapters 3 and 9.
notes.5:15: The Greek states that Hiram sent his servants 'to anoint Solomon,' whereas the Hebrew states that he sent them because he had heard that Solomon had been anointed king.
notes.5:25: 'Macheir' is an untranslated Greek transliteration corresponding to Hebrew 'makkolet' (food or provisions); the Greek also reads 'twenty thousand baths' of oil where the Hebrew reads 'twenty kors.'
notes.6:1: The Greek dates the temple's founding to the 'four hundred and fortieth year' of the Exodus (Hebrew: 'four hundred and eightieth') and gives the month names as 'Neiso' and 'Baad' (corresponding to Hebrew 'Ziv' and 'Bul'), combining foundation and completion notices in a single opening verse.
notes.6:2: The Greek gives the temple's length as 'forty cubits' and its height as 'twenty-five cubits,' whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text gives sixty cubits and thirty cubits respectively.
notes.6:3: 'Vestibule' translates Greek 'ailam' (a transliteration of Hebrew 'ulam'); similarly, in verse 5 and throughout the chapter, 'inner sanctuary' translates Greek 'dabeir' (Hebrew 'debir').
notes.6:21: 'Sealed gold' renders Greek 'chrysio synkekleismeno' (literally 'enclosed' or 'shut-up gold'), a literal rendering of Hebrew 'zahav sagur' denoting pure, choice treasury gold.
notes.6:26: The Greek text omits the numeral 'ten' here, stating only that the height of each cherub was measured 'by the cubit' (compare the ten-cubit stature stated in verse 23).
notes.7:3: The Greek transliterates the architectural term for the porch as ailam throughout the chapter and gives the pillar circumference as fourteen cubits, compared with twelve cubits in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.7:7: The Greek text gives the distinct pillar names Jachum (Iachoum) and Balaz, corresponding to Jachin and Boaz in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, and designates them simply as the one pillar and the second pillar.
notes.7:10: The Greek reads from its wall to its brim and gives a circumference of thirty-three cubits, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads from brim to brim and thirty cubits.
notes.7:14: Bases renders the Greek transliteration mechonoth used through verse twenty-nine; the Greek also records the dimensions as five cubits by four cubits by six cubits.
notes.7:33: Seira is the Greek text's distinct proper name for the location corresponding to Zarethan in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.8:2: Greek Athamein corresponds to Hebrew Ethanim (the seventh month); here and in 8:1 (which adds "after twenty years" and locates the assembly "in Zion") the Septuagint differs notably in detail and length from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.8:7: The Septuagint reads "its holy things" here and "the consecrated things" in 8:8 (Greek ta hagia / ta hegiasmena) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "its poles"; in 8:6 and 8:8 "inner sanctuary" translates Greek dabeir (transliterated Hebrew debir).
notes.8:11: Verses 8:12–13 are absent at this point in the Septuagint; the corresponding poetic declaration by Solomon appears after 8:53 in the Greek tradition.
notes.8:28: Greek tes terpseos ("the delight") reflects the joyful sense of Hebrew rinnah ("ringing cry" or "shout of joy").
notes.8:41: The Septuagint has a briefer text in 8:41–42 than the Hebrew Masoretic Text, omitting the clause describing the foreigner coming from a distant country on account of the Lord's great name and mighty hand.
notes.8:53: At the close of 8:53 the Septuagint places Solomon's poetic saying (corresponding to 8:12–13 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text), uniquely preserving the line "The Lord has made known the sun in heaven," reading "Build my house, a splendid house for Yourself, to dwell in anew," and citing "the Book of the Song" (Greek biblio tes odes).
notes.8:63: The Septuagint lists only "twenty-two thousand oxen" here, without the "one hundred and twenty thousand sheep" present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.8:65: The Septuagint adds "in the house which he had built, eating and drinking and rejoicing before the Lord our God" and specifies only "seven days" rather than the fourteen days of the Hebrew Masoretic Text; in 8:66 it similarly reads "he blessed them" rather than "they blessed the king."
notes.9:6: The Greek text reads "which Moses set before you," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "which I have set before you"; in 9:2 the Greek also has the place-name Gabaoth for Hebrew Gibeon.
notes.9:9: The Greek attaches the notice of Pharaoh's daughter (corresponding to 9:24 in the Hebrew) to the end of 9:9 and omits verses 15–25 here, placing much of the building and forced-labor account in 10:22.
notes.9:13: The Greek translates the Hebrew place-name Cabul as Horion ("Border").
notes.9:26: The Greek reads Emaeseion Gaber (for Hebrew Ezion Geber) and "the farthest sea" (for Hebrew "Sea of Reeds"), and in 9:28 names the destination Sophera (for Ophir) with one hundred and twenty talents of gold (Hebrew: four hundred and twenty).
notes.10:8: The Greek reads "your wives" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "your men," reflecting a difference in vocalizing the Hebrew consonants.
notes.10:11: The Greek reads Souphir (for Hebrew Ophir) and renders Hebrew almug wood here and in 10:12 as "hewn timber."
notes.10:16: The Greek reads three hundred spears of beaten gold with three hundred pieces of gold per spear, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads two hundred large shields with six hundred shekels of gold per shield.
notes.10:22: The Greek reads "engraved and hewn stones" (for Hebrew "ivory, apes, and peacocks") and places here the account of Solomon's levy and fortifications (cf. Hebrew 9:15–22), with distinctive place-names Assour, Midian, Upper Baithoram, and Iethermath (for Hebrew Hazor, Megiddo, Lower Beth-horon, and Tamar).
notes.10:29: The Greek reads one hundred and fifty pieces of silver (Hebrew: six hundred and one hundred and fifty) and "by sea" (Hebrew: "by their hand"), following 10:26 ("four thousand mares for chariots") and 10:28 (Thekoue for Hebrew Kue).
notes.11:5: The Greek renders the Ammonite deity Milcom (or Molech) literally as "their king" and orders verses 5–8 differently from the Hebrew text; verse 3 is absent because the count of Solomon's princesses and concubines appears in verse 1.
notes.11:14: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew word for "adversary" as satan, preserves the distinct names Ader (Hebrew Hadad) and Esrom (Hebrew Rezon), combines the material of Hebrew verses 23–24 into this verse, and reads "who was in Raemmaaer" where the Hebrew has "who fled from."
notes.11:19: The Greek gives the Egyptian queen's name as Thekemina (Hebrew Tahpenes), and later preserves the distinct names Sarira (11:26, 43; Hebrew Zeredah) and Susakim (11:40; Hebrew Shishak).
notes.11:32: The Greek reads "two tribes" here and in verse 36 (using skeptra, literally "scepters"), whereas verse 13 and the Hebrew text read "one tribe."
notes.11:34: The Greek reads "I will surely oppose him" where the Hebrew has "I will make him ruler," and in verse 36 uses thesis ("an established place") where the Hebrew has "a lamp."
notes.12:18: The Greek names the officer over the tribute Aram (Hebrew Adoram) and does not mention a chariot in Rehoboam's escape.
notes.12:20: The Greek text explicitly reads "Rehoboam" here (where the Hebrew and narrative context have "Jeroboam"), and specifies "the tribe of Judah and Benjamin alone" rather than Judah alone.
notes.12:24: Following the standard verse 24, the Greek includes an extensive alternative narrative (often designated 12:24a–z) detailing Rehoboam's reign (age sixteen, reigning twelve years; mother Naanan), Jeroboam's mother Sarisa, his marriage to Ano (sister of Thekemina), the death of his child Abijah, and a garment-tearing sign performed by Shemaiah the Enlamite ("twelve pieces" concerning "the ten tribes").
notes.12:28: The Greek reads "two golden heifers" (damaleis) rather than "calves," and in verse 27 explicitly names both "the Lord" (God) and "their lord" (Rehoboam).
notes.13:3: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew consecutive verb as a future tense ("will give") and reads "the word" (Hebrew "the sign") and "the fatness" (Hebrew "the ashes").
notes.13:11: The Septuagint reads "and they turned the face of their father," diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("and they recounted them to their father").
notes.13:26: The Septuagint preserves a shorter text here, omitting the remainder of verse 26 and all of verse 27 found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.13:31: The Septuagint reads "after lamenting him" (Hebrew "after burying him") and adds the purpose clause "so that my bones may be saved with his bones."
notes.14:21: The Old Greek omits verses 1–20 (placing the story of Jeroboam's son in 12:24g–n) and names Rehoboam's mother Maacham, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has Naamah.
notes.14:24: The Septuagint reads "a conspiracy" (Greek syndesmos), diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("male cult prostitutes").
notes.14:26: The Septuagint adds the golden spears David captured from the servants of Hadarezer king of Zobah (cf. 2 Samuel 8:7) and omits the Hebrew reference to shields made by Solomon.
notes.14:27: The Greek verb is plural ("placed themselves over him"), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("he committed them into the hands of the captains of the guards").
notes.14:31: The Septuagint names Rehoboam's son Abiu, corresponding to Abijam in the Hebrew Masoretic Text of Kings (and Abijah in Chronicles).
notes.15:1: The Greek text identifies Abiu (Hebrew Abijam/Abijah) as the son of Jeroboam rather than Rehoboam, and in verse 2 gives his reign as six years rather than three.
notes.15:10: Here and in verse 13 the Greek gives the queen mother's name as Ana where the Hebrew reads Maachah; verse 13 also renders the Kidron Valley literally as "the brook of the cedars."
notes.15:18: The Greek literally translates the name Ben-Hadad as "the son of Hader" (here and in verse 20) and omits the treasuries of the house of the Lord; verse 20 also preserves the distinct Greek place names Ain, Adelmath, and Chezrath.
notes.15:22: The Greek treats the Hebrew phrase "none was exempted" as a place name ("to Enakim") and translates Geba and Mizpah as common nouns ("every hill" and "the watchtower").
notes.15:25: Here and in verses 27 and 31 the Greek gives the name of Jeroboam's son as Nebat (matching Jeroboam's father) where the Hebrew reads Nadab; in verse 27 the Greek also reads "the house of Belaan" where the Hebrew reads "the house of Issachar."
notes.16:9: The Greek names the steward Osa (Hebrew Arza); in verse 15 the Greek gives Zimri's reign as seven years (Hebrew seven days) and places the camp at Gibeon rather than Gibbethon.
notes.16:16: Throughout verses 16 through 29, the Greek text reads the name Zimri where the Hebrew introduces Omri as the army commander, king of Israel, and father of Ahab.
notes.16:22: The Greek adds that Tibni's brother Joram also died at that time.
notes.16:28: The Greek places the summary of Jehoshaphat's reign here (paralleling 1 Kings 22:41-50 in the Hebrew), with distinct readings including "Gabuza, daughter of Selei," "Syria" (Hebrew Edom), "Sophir" (Hebrew Ophir), and the transliterated Hebrew title "Nasib" (meaning "deputy").
notes.16:33: Where the Hebrew states that Ahab provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger, the Greek reads that he provoked "his own soul, so as to be utterly destroyed."
notes.17:1: The Greek text adds "the prophet" and "the God of hosts," identifies Elijah as coming "from Tishbe of Gilead" (Greek Thesbon), and renders the closing phrase literally as "by the mouth of my word."
notes.17:12: Here and in verses 13 and 15, the Greek text reads plural "children" rather than singular "son" as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.17:20: The Greek text addresses the Lord as "the witness of the widow" and frames Elijah's cry as a direct exclamation rather than a question.
notes.17:21: The Greek reads "breathed upon the child three times" (rather than "stretched himself upon the child" in the Hebrew), and verse 22 concisely reports that "the child cried out."
notes.18:10: The Greek text states that Ahab "burned the kingdom and its regions," whereas the Hebrew reads that he made the kingdom or nation swear an oath.
notes.18:19: Here and in verse 25, the Greek substitutes "shame" for Baal (and "abominations" in verse 29), and renders Asherah as "the groves" (or "grove" in verse 22).
notes.18:29: Rather than stating that no one answered, the Greek records Elijah instructing the prophets of the abominations to stand aside so that he may prepare his burnt offering, followed by their departure.
notes.18:32: Here and in verses 35 and 38, the Greek uses thalassa ("sea") for the water trench or basin around the altar, echoing the bronze sea of the temple.
notes.18:45: Here and in verse 46, the Greek reads "Israel" instead of "Jezreel" (as in the Hebrew), and in verse 45 reports that Ahab "wept" rather than "rode."
notes.19:2: The Greek opens Jezebel's oath with "If you are Elijah and I am Jezebel" and refers to "God" in the singular, whereas the Masoretic Text omits the opening clause and reads "the gods."
notes.19:11: Following Codex Vaticanus, this Greek text adds "tomorrow" and reads "in the wind of the Lord" without the negation ("the Lord was not in the wind") found in the Masoretic Text and other Septuagint manuscripts; verse 12 renders the famous Hebrew phrase as "the sound of a gentle breeze."
notes.19:16: Following Codex Vaticanus, this Greek text reads "the son of Jehu, the son of Nimshi" rather than "Jehu the son of Nimshi," though verse 17 names Jehu directly.
notes.19:18: The Greek reads second-person "you shall leave" (where the Masoretic Text has first-person "I have reserved") and "worshiped" (where the Masoretic Text has "kissed").
notes.19:20: The Greek reads "for I have done this to you" as a statement rather than the Masoretic Text's rhetorical question ("for what have I done to you?").
notes.20:1: In the Septuagint, the account of Naboth's vineyard stands as chapter 20 (chapter 21 in the Masoretic Text), consistently calls Naboth "the Israelite" rather than "the Jezreelite" (compare "Israel" in verse 23), and places the vineyard beside Ahab's "threshing floor" rather than his palace.
notes.20:10: Following Codex Vaticanus, this Greek text ends Jezebel's quoted letter here, omitting the further instructions to accuse and stone Naboth that appear in the Masoretic Text and other Greek witnesses.
notes.20:13: "You have blessed God and the king" preserves the literal Greek rendering of the traditional Hebrew euphemism for cursing God and the king.
notes.20:16: The Greek uniquely records Ahab tearing his garments and putting on sackcloth immediately upon hearing of Naboth's death (compare verse 27, where he goes about weeping and puts on sackcloth on the day he struck down Naboth).
notes.20:19: The Greek adds "the swine" alongside the dogs and includes the prophecy that "the harlots shall wash themselves in your blood," anticipating the fulfillment in 1 Kings 22:38.
notes.21:1: The Septuagint reverses the order of chapters 20 and 21 relative to the Hebrew Masoretic Text and renders the Aramean royal name Ben-Hadad literally as Son of Hader (Greek huios Hader, reflecting an r/d interchange at the end of the name).
notes.21:10: The Greek reads for the foxes (tais alopexin), translating the Hebrew consonants for handfuls (she'alim) as foxes (shu'alim).
notes.21:11: Where the Hebrew proverb speaks of one who puts on armor not boasting like one who takes it off, the Septuagint renders the saying as the hunchbacked (ho kyrtos) not boasting like the upright (ho orthos).
notes.21:18: Verses 18 and 19 feature elliptical Greek syntax with imperatival infinitives (Tell them... seize them alive) and a negative command (do not let... come out) where the Hebrew narrates that the young men went out.
notes.21:40: The Septuagint preserves a markedly different reply from Ahab (Behold, you have even slain the ambushes beside me) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads, So shall your judgment be; you yourself have decided it.
notes.22:10: The Septuagint describes the kings as sitting armed in the gates of Samaria rather than clothed in robes at a threshing floor as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text. In verses 8-9, 11, and 24, the Greek also preserves the distinct name forms Jemiah (Hebrew Imlah), Chaana, and Canaan (Hebrew Chenaanah).
notes.22:16: The Greek reads 'Five times' rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'How many times,' and in verse 17 renders the Lord's declaration as 'Is the Lord not God to these?' instead of 'These have no master.'
notes.22:26: The Septuagint identifies the city official as 'Semer the king of the city,' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'Amon the governor of the city.'
notes.22:34: The Greek states that the archer drew his bow 'with good aim' and struck Ahab 'between the lung and the breastplate,' contrasting with the Hebrew 'at random' and 'between the joints of his armor.' Similarly, verse 30 has Ahab instruct Jehoshaphat to put on 'my robes,' and verse 38 adds 'the swine' alongside the dogs.
notes.22:42: The Septuagint gives the name of Jehoshaphat's mother as 'Azaeba, the daughter of Shimei,' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has 'Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.'
